audit.note: the three anchors open the hidden DynamicDateRange roundtrip-free via follow_up_action( control_by_id, openBy, $event.oSource.sId ) (the app 016 DatePickerHidden idiom); the change handler round-trips operator, value count and the first two values, and the backend composes the toast

deviations.what: the sap.m.DynamicDateRange control (since UI5 1.92.0) is newer than 1.71 and is the whole point of this sample - kept 1:1, the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.92.0.
DynamicDateRange.hideInput and DynamicDateRange.openBy (both since UI5 1.105) are the sample's central mechanism - kept 1:1, the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.105.
Button.ariaHasPopup (since UI5 1.84) is kept 1:1 on both Button controls - the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.84 to render it.
Link.ariaHasPopup (since UI5 1.86) is kept 1:1 - the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.86 to render it.

changeDateHandler's MessageToast is composed in ABAP (on_event CHANGE) instead of in the controller: the wire carries ${$parameters>/value/operator}, the values count and values[0]/values[1] (no standard option has more than two values), each value as `<value> + ''` so a Date arrives as its toString and a boolean 'included' flag as true/false - exactly what the original's string concatenation prints.

unverified in a running system: the openBy anchor opening the hidden DynamicDateRange popover (app 016's hidden DatePicker loops in Popover.onfocusin HEADLESS only), and the `${$parameters>/value/values/0} + ''` string-concatenation event args reaching the toast. **e2e-verified 2026-10-20** (nightly e2e interaction, meta/interactions/z2ui5_cl_smpc_app_641.mjs).

e2e_smoke.reason: unthemed, the hidden DynamicDateRange popover opened by openBy loops in Popover.onfocusin (focus restore bounces off the hidden input) until the stack overflows - the original openBy(getDomRef()) does the same headless; themed it opens cleanly and the interaction drives the pick
